ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC SDN list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury, EU Consolidated List, SADC terrorism list, and South African domestic sanctions register under POCDATARA. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is statutorily required for all politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates, in line with FICA sections 20A-20D and the Financial Intelligence Centre Directive.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under regulation 9 of the Companies Regulations, 2011, a company name may be in any official South African language but must be expressed in the Latin (Roman) alphabet; non-Latin scripts require transliteration. The name must end with an appropriate corporate designation such as "(Pty) Ltd" and may not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, nor contrary to public policy or morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of name rejection by CIPC under s. 11(2)(b) of the Companies Act, the applicant may file a formal objection with CIPC within 15 business days of receipt of the refusal, requesting reconsideration under regulation 14(4). If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for a review within 30 days after the refusal notice. Parties aggrieved by a Companies Tribunal decision may approach the High Court for judicial review. The appeal must be submitted via the CIPC e-services portal using Form CIPC/CO/1, accompanied by a sworn affidavit, the original rejection notice, and supporting evidence of any corrective action.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for registered-office purposes provided it constitutes a physical registered address in South Africa, not a post office box, capable of receiving and storing legal correspondence. For the scrap-metal trading industry, regulators including SAPS and SARS may require demonstrated operational substance (e.g., a storage yard, inspection facility, or physical place of business) beyond a virtual office; therefore, a fully virtual arrangement is unlikely to satisfy licensing requirements under the Second-Hand Goods Act and may increase AML/CFT compliance scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high: approximately 60% statistical likelihood of unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation, escalating to 80% during scrap-metal licence application and first-year operations, based on sectoral enforcement data for non-ferrous scrap dealers under SAPS and SARS supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Proprietary Limited Company; shares are authorised and issued as zero-par-value ordinary shares; no escrow or capitalised deposit account is required under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first meeting of the board of directors of [Company Name] (Pty) Ltd held on [date] and at [location] as follows: (1) The allotment and issue of the subscribers' ordinary shares as recorded in the Memorandum of Incorporation and initial share register is ratified. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Memorandum of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC E-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za), Name Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services and complete Form CoR 9.1 requesting reservation of the company name; pay the name reservation fee; upon issuance of CoR 9.6 (Name Reservation Certificate), draft the Memorandum of Incorporation based on the Model MOI (Form CoR 15.1C), incorporating amendments for authorised share capital and director powers; have every incorporator sign the MOI and the initial share subscription agreement.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1 name reservation application
Certified copies of incorporators' identity documents (South African citizens) or passport/visa copies (non-resident incorporators)
Draft Memorandum of Incorporation
Proof of proposed registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
Signed share subscription agreement for the initial allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC refuses or queries the proposed name, lodge a fresh name reservation application or apply for a name change under Section 160(2) of the Companies Act; no notarisation of the MOI is required under South African law, but any CIPC-formality defect must be corrected and re-lodged within the compliance window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) through BizPortal / e-Services; physical office at 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Form CoR 14.1A (Notice of Incorporation) as the statutory filing instrument; attach the signed Memorandum of Incorporation, the Name Reservation Certificate, and the consent of each first director to act; submit the full dossier via CIPC e-Services or at a CIPC Business Centre; pay the prescribed R175 registration fee; await issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and the unique company registration number.
required_dossiers: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A) signed by the incorporator
Signed Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
Name Reservation Certificate (CoR 9.6)
Consent to Appointment as First Director (Form CoR 16.1A or equivalent signed consent clause)
Identity numbers or passport copies of the first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a notice of defective filing, rectify the specified defect and re-lodge within the statutory correction period; the date of incorporation is the later of the date on the Certificate of Incorporation or the date stated in the Notice of Incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Statutory Register Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (issuance of CoR 14.1); the company's directors establish and maintain statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, download and retain the Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) from CIPC e-Services; open the statutory records: share register, register of directors, register of company secretaries, and register of beneficial ownership; submit the beneficial ownership notice (Form TMO) to CIPC within 10 business days of the securities register entry; convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, recording it in duly signed minutes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Initial office-holder consents and director declarations
Completed beneficial ownership schedule (Form TMO)
Statutory share register and equity ledger
First board meeting minutes signed by the chairperson
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC flags non-filing of the beneficial ownership notice, submit Form TMO immediately to restore good standing; an inadvertent omission is curable by lodging a supplementary notice together with the prescribed late filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration, UIF/COIDA Compliance and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); Department of Employment and Labour; commercial banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Income Tax through SARS eFiling using the company registration number and director details; obtain a SARS Income Tax reference number; apply for VAT registration where annual turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed R1,000,000 (voluntary registration permissible from R50,000); register as an employer for PAYE, UIF, and COIDA worker's compensation; open the corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, MOI, and the adopted board resolution appointing a bank mandate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
SARS company registration application submitted via eFiling
Board resolution specifying the bank mandate and signatories
Proof of registered office address and certified directors' identity documents
COIDA registration acknowledgment and annual letter of good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or queries the registration, verify the taxpayer PIN, correct the directors' records, and re-submit through eFiling; the COIDA Letter of Good Standing is issued electronically within 21 days once the annual return is complete; any bank-file discrepancy is cured by a supplemental board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Scrap Metal Dealer Registration under the Second-Hand Goods Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Police Service (SAPS), Crime Prevention Divisions (Second-Hand Goods Office) at the police station having jurisdiction over the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for registration as a dealer in second-hand goods and scrap metal under the Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009 at the relevant SAPS station; submit the registration form, supporting documents and the prescribed fee; obtain the issuance of the Scrap Metal Dealer Registration Certificate before commencing trading; maintain the mandatory second-hand goods register recording every acquisition and disposal of copper wire scrap; notify SAPS of any change of premises and renew the certificate annually.
required_dossiers: SAPS Second-Hand Goods Authority registration application form
Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Proof of ownership or lease of the registered business premises
Police clearance certificates for all directors and the manager
SARS Tax Clearance Certificate and municipal business licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or refused, invoke Sections 19-24 of the Second-Hand Goods Act and appeal through the National Commissioner of Police, with further review by the High Court if necessary; pending registration, physical possession of scrap copper wire must be limited to the named premises under controlled conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Police Service (SAPS) under the Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009; National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS) for metal quality conformance; municipal licensing authority for the local business licence
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Scrap Metal Dealer Registration Certificate (Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009, Section 4) together with the Municipal Business Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment and Waste Licensing
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Basic Assessment under Listing Notice 1 (GN R983) for a scrap storage and wholesale yard; full EIA is not triggered absent smelting, leaching or mechanical shredding beyond simple stripping; a Waste Management Licence may be required under the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008 only if the site is classified as a waste disposal facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero untreated discharge to surface water; National Water Act 36 of 1998, Section 21(1)(i) water use licence for any waste water disposal; National Dust Control Regulations, 2013 (GN R827) dust fallout limit of 600 mg/m²/day in residential areas; atmospheric emissions must not exceed the Listed Activities thresholds under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004; stripped insulation and cutting residues are to be classified, segregated and manifested as non-hazardous waste under NEM:WA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificate of Fire Safety Compliance issued by the municipal Fire Protection Services under SANS 10400-T of the National Building Regulations; structural load certification for racking systems issued by an approved inspection body; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 workplace clearance and incident-reporting compliance; COIDA letter of good standing; annual evacuation and emergency preparedness inspection for the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — statutory tax and customs authority; principal taxpayer portal is SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); corporate registry interface is CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) via https://www.cipc.co.za; customs and export declarations are lodged electronically through the SARS Customs EDAN/SAD500 e-filing systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Pty Ltd: (1) incorporate the private company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 at CIPC to obtain the unique company registration number, using the CIPC-SARS one-stop registration data channel; (2) complete SARS income tax registration through eFiling or at a SARS branch to obtain the income tax reference number; (3) file VAT registration via eFiling (Form VAT 101) with a declaration of current and projected annual taxable turnover; compulsory VAT registration applies when taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed R 1,000,000 per annum, and SARS will issue a VAT vendor number; (4) apply to SARS Customs for an importer/exporter customs code before moving goods; (5) file beneficial ownership information with CIPC and complete SARS activation requirements. For a foreign entity earning South African source income or making South African taxable supplies: register as an external company with CIPC if it carries on business in South Africa, obtain a SARS income tax reference number, and register as a foreign vendor under s 50A of the VAT Act once South African taxable supplies exceed the R 1,000,000 threshold; a South African tax representative (TAA s 251) may be required for fiscal compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Pty Ltd is a legal person and company taxed as a separate taxable entity under s 1 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and the Companies Act 71 of 2008; resident companies are taxed on worldwide income at the 27% normal corporate income tax rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (28% in prior years); there is no look-through or pass-through taxation of shareholders for corporate income tax; distributions are separately subject to dividends tax at 20% (subject to treaty relief and the s 64FA exemptions). Export profit from scrap copper sales is ordinary taxable income in South Africa, and foreign exchange gains are taxable (or losses deductible) when accounted for under the functional currency rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box regime, but the following statutory elections are relevant to a cross-border scrap exporter: (1) headquarter company election under s 9I of the Income Tax Act, giving conduit treatment for qualifying foreign dividends, interest, royalties and CFC proceeds; (2) controlled foreign company elections under s 9D, including the high-tax exemption election (foreign effective tax at least 90% of South African normal tax), the voluntary inclusion election under s 9D(9A), and the foreign business establishment active-income exclusion; (3) conduit arrangement election under s 12B for foreign entities or partnerships substantially similar to South African partnerships, enabling transparent taxation of members; (4) VAT group registration election under s 50(1) of the VAT Act; (5) corporate reorganisation rollover elections under ss 45-46 of the Income Tax Act for tax-neutral asset-for-share and amalgamation transactions in metals supply chains; and (6) trading-stock valuation elections under s 22(1) for scrap inventory employing base stock, FIFO, weighted average or specific identification methods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, as amended. Exchange control is operationally delegated to Authorised Dealers, being the South African commercial banks approved by SARB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa applies a controlled convertibility regime rather than full free convertibility. Current-account trade transactions, including payment of bona fide import/export obligations and trade-related expenses, are normally permissible through an authorised dealer without prior SARB approval once supporting contracts and SARS customs documentation are presented. Capital-account inflows, such as foreign direct investment and shareholder loans, are operationally welcome but must be reported and registered with the authorised dealer; capital-account outflows by residents, offshore investments by residents, and certain non-resident credit/guarantee structures remain exchange-control restricted. Profit remittances are permissible where there is evidence of after-tax distributable profits, audited or management financial statements, a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status/PIN, settlement of dividends tax at 20% or reduced treaty rate, and, if the capital was originally imported, proof of the inward transfer through the authorised dealer. The ZAR is not a fully externally convertible currency, but an active offshore NDF market exists and authorised dealers may offer appropriate hedging to residents with a documented underlying trade exposure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in full within 180 days from the date of shipment unless the authorised dealer has approved alternative payment terms. The exporter must submit the relevant SARS export declaration (SAD500) and shipping documents, and all foreign currency proceeds received by the South African exporting entity must be surrendered to an authorised dealer for conversion into rand unless a SARB/FinSurv-approved foreign-currency retention account exists. If no such account is approved, surrender is required within 30 days of receipt, and the default statutory position is 100% conversion of export proceeds into ZAR. Overdue export proceeds are reportable by the authorised dealer to FinSurv, and any write-off, reinvoicing, discount, or non-receipt of proceeds requires full documented justification and, where applicable, prior approval or tolerance from the authorised dealer.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, or Payoneer are not authorised dealers under the South African Exchange Control Regulations and do not hold a South African banking licence. They cannot serve as the primary clearing or surrender rail for export proceeds because those proceeds must be received through an authorised dealer and surrendered to the local banking system. Such EMIs may be used only as an ancillary collection or payment interface provided the final, regulated settlement remains in a SARB-licensed authorised dealer account. Holding funds offshore in an EMI without FinSurv approval, or routing export proceeds to an EMI instead of the authorised dealer, would constitute an exchange-control contravention and may trigger account closure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, the bank must identify and verify the corporate client, all directors, and all beneficial owners before account opening. South African resident directors may generally complete FICA verification remotely through biometric liveness checks and submission of certified identity documents. Non-resident directors and beneficial owners are subject to enhanced due diligence and, in the medium-risk scrap-metal sector, most tier-one banks require a physical or consular-attested interview before unlimited transactional activity is permitted. Apostilled/certified passports, proof of residential address, source of wealth, source of funds, and FATCA/CRS self-certifications are mandatory. Full remote opening cannot be assumed; where remote opening is initially accepted, the bank may place temporary limits on outbound transactions until the non-resident principals complete the interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-level red flag: non-ferrous scrap dealing and recycling is treated by banks as a metal-theft and money-laundering sensitive industry; the account application may be declined if the applicant cannot evidence a lawful, auditable supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAPS registration/licence as a second-hand scrap-metal dealer under the Second-Hand Goods Act 6 of 2009 and the Non-Ferrous Metals Theft Prevention Act 4 of 2019; ITAC scrap-metal export permit where applicable; purchase ledger with itemised supplier invoices; weighbridge tickets; supplier identification and source-of-title declarations; transport manifests; insurance policy; independent due-diligence report confirming no stolen-metal or conflict-material links.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: non-resident shareholders, nominee shareholders, or trust structures prevent the bank from determining the natural persons owning or controlling ZA Pty Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Companies Register extract and beneficial-ownership lodgement acknowledgement; register of members; trust deed or nominee declaration; sworn affidavits; official photo ID and passports; proof of residential address; prior bank references; corporate structure chart; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Price or invoice integrity risk: declared unit price diverges materially from prevailing LME copper/scrap indices, or shipping and title documents conflict with the stated payment terms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed trade contract with Incoterms 2020; LME pricing formula or broker statement; independent pre-shipment surveyor's certificate; laboratory assay/report; bill of lading or air waybill; SARS customs declaration SAD500; packing list and cargo manifest; bank trade-document checking record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement or non-correspondent payment routing: counterparty proposes payment from an entity other than the contracting party, or uses an EMI/crypto channel that obscures the SWIFT MT103 trace.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group holding or affiliation evidence; agency, back-to-back, or intercompany agreement explaining the payor; full SWIFT gpi MT103/MT202 message including correspondent route; completed counterparty KYC pack; documented rejection of non-bank or crypto funding; confirmation that all proceeds are credited directly to the ZA entity's authorised-dealer account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act Section 33 / CIPC Regulation 55)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty accrues at ZAR 300 (approx USD 16) per month or part thereof; two consecutive unfiled annual returns trigger section 71 deregistration proceedings and director disqualification risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (integrated with Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as Annual Return; any beneficial ownership change requiring updated filing must be lodged within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a current UBO register is a contravention of section 56 of the Companies Act; persistent non-compliance may result in CIPC enforcement action, financial penalties, and administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements (only if mandatory audit threshold is triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit audited annual financial statements violates section 33; CIPC may issue an enforcement notice and hold directors personally liable for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit required when the public interest score (PIS) equals or exceeds 500; PIS between 100 and 349 generally requires an independent review (unless audit is voluntarily elected or required by the memorandum of incorporation); PIS between 350 and 499 requires a review but audit may be voluntarily elected. Companies classified as 'societally significant' must be audited. PIS below 100 requires neither audit nor review if the financial statements are internally prepared.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS for public-interest companies and where voluntarily adopted; IFRS for SMEs for eligible private companies; all financial statements must comply with Companies Act Sections 28-29 and Financial Reporting Standards Council approved standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Pty Ltd must maintain a register of beneficial ownership and file the annual confirmation together with the CIPC Annual Return. Share transfers or changes in beneficial ownership must be recorded and lodged with CIPC within 10 business days. The annual confirmation must declare all ultimate beneficial owners and any changes since the last filing, supported by identity attestation documentation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $350–$900 per year (typical registered office plus CIPC annual return filing service by a licensed company secretary or registered agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,000–$15,000 per audit for a small or medium Pty Ltd with international trade flows and recycled scrap copper wire consignment operations
